original_context_note: Compared spec.full_target literally with target-selection.json/full_target and problem.md:21-30: the complete selected target, Euclidean metric, interval endpoints and n=0 case are retained. A nonnegative integer is represented by a natural number; H001 still explicitly states n≥0 and is retained as the sole unused original H, rather than inventing a use. H002 is the disclosed approved nonemptiness condition (problem.md:16-23), and H003 is precisely compactness; no conclusion or proof claim is an H. H002 is actually used in R002/S002 and R009/S001, and H003 in R002/S001. D001 supplies the actual Euclidean squared-distance metric, including V(0); R002/S003 proves the concatenation isometry rather than silently changing to the native max-product metric. D002 is the total extended diameter; finite real diameters are used only after a finite scale bounds them. D003 retains the exact original covering infimum, countability, empty-member convention and supremum over positive scales; only the trailing incomplete word from the copied passage was removed. D004-D005 use the native gauge measure and native supremum definition of dimension: pinned Hausdorff.lean:535-552 and HausdorffDimension.lean:94-135 were read, and R001 proves the positive-exponent normalization bridge. D006-D008 define I,F,D without granting dimension or finiteness properties; finiteness of D is proved in N002 before subsequent real-exponent limits. D009 is the finite-open-subcover definition actually used in R002, not a compactness conclusion hidden in a definition. D010-D012 specify the measure, lower integral and indicators; no measurability of arbitrary covering sets is assumed. Construction guards were checked at R003/S001-S002 (q>0 and n≥1 before the small positive balls), R004/S002 (positive r_i before division and the ceiling), R005/S002 (nonempty bounded B before the real infimum/supremum), and R006/S001-S003 (finite c, finite nonnegative diameters, positive error denominators and Borel intervals before integration). All 13 M declarations have successful same-stage probes with pinned signatures and official-source readback: M001-M005 in the Hausdorff files; M006-M008 in Lebesgue Add/Basic; M009-M010 in Lebesgue Basic; M011 in OuterMeasure Basic; M012-M013 in Pow Continuity/Asymptotics. Their NL statements preserve native measurable/Borel, extended-metric, countability, almost-everywhere measurability, order and exponent premises. The initially guessed namespace for M013 failed and was replaced by the actually probed unnamespaced theorem. Ordered attempts to retrieve the cited Stein-Shakarchi book were unsuccessful and are preserved in the access records; that book is not an imported theorem root, and no inaccessible-primary assumption or unverified E is used. Principal tools are supplied by the verified native sources instead. The graph has 25 propositions and nine producers; all selected M and all eight N are in P's backward AND closure, while H001 is explicitly reported unused. R002-R009 follow every required phase of problem.md:49-167: bounded-dimension grid, singleton replacements, interval product covers with the factor 2(√2)^{q+1}, same-scale slicing with η_i=ε2^{-i-1}/(1+ρ_i^s), Tonelli, error removal and infimum, the s↑D limit, and the interval/isometric-fibre treatment of D=0 including n=0. No needed calculation or limiting argument has been omitted. This is my own packet closing inspection, not independent Audit A; structural validation is not mathematical certification.

output_notes.note: R001/S001 and F001 export the exact equality between the supplied H and native μH at every positive exponent, the direction of scale monotonicity, and the unbounded-small-scale implication. S002/F002 establish all four critical-exponent implications with their strict ranges. S003 proves inclusion monotonicity and isometric-image invariance from covers, including equality of ambient contents for maps defined only on the set. S004 establishes the two signed power limits and the two exact geometric-series values. The N001 statement includes all these formulas, not just theorem names; no consumer needs R001's body.

R002/S001 exports boundedness and finite contents for every s,δ>0, with compactness supplying the finite subcovers. S002 constructs the cube grid and proves 0≤D≤n, and separately proves E=V(0), D=0 when n=0 using H002. S003 supplies the actual inverse and squared-distance identity for the concatenation isometry. Each of these clauses appears in N002, including the metric identification used by P.

R003/S001 obtains the initial cost <ε/2 cover by the scale infimum, with q>0 grounded in N002. S002 supplies an explicit positive-diameter replacement for every singleton and bounds its q-cost by ε2^{-i-2}; the total added budget is at most ε/2. The exported statement quantifies all q>D, 0<r≤1, ε>0 under n≥1, and includes countability, coverage, nonemptiness, the identity r_i=diam(U_i), positive radii, the scale bound and strict total cost <ε.

R004/S001 handles n=0 by equal interval pieces; S002 derives diam≤√2 r_i and Σ_iN_i(√2 r_i)^{q+1}≤2(√2)^{q+1}Σ_i r_i^q, at r=min(1,δ/√2). S003 closes ε, all scales, and q↓D, with D finite from N002. This proves the unconditional exported inequality dim_H(F)≤D+1 for every ambient case, not merely an estimate at one exponent.

R005/S001 proves the normalization λ(I)=1. S002 proves the nonempty bounded-set guard, α=inf B and β=sup B with β-α≤ρ, and gives the explicit interval J=(α-η/2,β+η/2). It proves containment, the length and measure bounds, and Borel measurability of J and J∩I. These are all exported in N005 so that the slicing and interval-cover consumers can construct J without importing this producer body.

R006/S001-S003 construct the projected covers and Borel majorants without assuming measurability of W_i or their projections, and prove the global indicator inequality. S004 gives c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}+ε with the original η_i and its summable weighted error. S005 first quantifies ε, treats the infinite-cost alternative, then takes the infimum over all covers. Thus N006 is exactly the same-scale inequality for every s>0,δ>0, with no omitted finiteness assumption on the product-cover cost.

R007/S001 uses N006 at every δ and N001 at 0<s<D to obtain H^{s+1}(F)=∞ and dim_H(F)≥s+1. S002 closes the arbitrary s and uses positive finite D from N002 to take its supremum. The exported conclusion retains D>0 as an antecedent; it does not assert this lower bound unconditionally.

R008/S001 proves H^a(I)=0 for every a>1. S002 proves Σ_iρ_i≥1 for every δ-cover by measurable open-interval enclosures and length subadditivity. S003 includes the zero-diameter case in ρ_i^s≥δ^{s-1}ρ_i, then infimizes and sends δ↓0 for 0<s<1. The output explicitly includes H^s_δ(I)≥δ^{s-1}, H^s(I)=∞ and dim_H(I)=1, so the final fibre argument has the exact interval-dimension conclusion.

R009/S001 combines N004 with N007 when D>0 and, when D=0, uses an H002 witness x_0, the map t↦(x_0,t), N001's isometric-image invariance/monotonicity and N008's dim_H(I)=1. N002 gives exhaustive nonnegative finite D and the Euclidean concatenation identification. Substituting D=dim_H(E) and F=E×I gives the complete spec.conclusion, including n=0 and the exact metric, without joining independent assumptions or weakening the target.
